A1.justification: Both 32-page PDFs describe CVE-Factory and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F. The references and appendices are identical in text and rendered appearance, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CVE reproduction experiments, model evaluations, and fine-tuning results in Section 4 and Tables 1, 3, and 7, with additional empirical analyses and case-study results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original reproduction experiments, model evaluations, fine-tuning results, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The six-stage reproduction pipeline, specialized agents, context isolation, feedback routing, verification procedures, and Qwen3-32B fine-tuning approach remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same PatchEval tasks, sampled May–December 2025 CVEs, LiveCVEBench, SETA training tasks, and Terminal-Bench evaluation. Language, vulnerability-type, domain, and temporal test coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: The PatchEval expert comparison, SETA-trained baseline, and evaluated model/framework combinations in Tables 3 and 7 are identical. No comparator is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Both retain 215 PatchEval CVEs after exclusions, 554 reproduction candidates, the 3k/4k trajectory settings, and five-epoch fine-tuning. Sampling procedures, validation criteria, evaluation metrics, and other experimental settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The temporal performance analysis in Figure 4, failure analysis in Table 6, Appendix C subgroup analyses, Appendix E resource analysis, and Appendix F comparative case study are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting remains unchanged, including Appendix C.1's mean and standard-deviation summary. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-test information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative findings are unchanged. Table 1 retains 95.35% solution correctness, 96.13% environment fidelity, and 73.91% test quality; Table 3 retains 35.79% LiveCVEBench performance for Qwen3-32B trained on CVE (4k). The appendix results also match.

T1.justification: Appendix B's scoring rules and composite sampling formula, Equation 1, are identical. No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both retain the same core claims: expert-level automated CVE task reproduction, LiveCVEBench, large-scale training-task synthesis, and generalization of security training to terminal tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning temporal drift, potential contamination, agent-framework effects, training generalization, and mock/static-test failures are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same qualifications about task-composition confounding and deployment issues.

D1.justification: v1's abstract links directly to CVE-Factory, LiveCVEBench, Abacus-cve, the training dataset, and the leaderboard. v2 removes these five resource destinations and substitutes a general open-source statement, reducing access guidance. Implementation examples and training details in Appendices A and D remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography are unchanged, including the positioning relative to CVE-Genie and automated software-engineering task generators.

P1.justification: The author line changes Rain Huang to Jinyang Huang, the preprint footer becomes ICML/PMLR proceedings text, and the abstract's resource statement is shortened. Section 4.2.3 changes its correct Figure 4 reference to an incorrect Figure 6 reference. The substantive narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is reduced in size, Figure 2 is rescaled/reformatted, and main-text page breaks shift. All six figures and ten tables are retained with the same substantive content; appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: The scientific content is unchanged, but v2 removes direct resource links and introduces an incorrect cross-reference: Section 4.2.3 points to Figure 6's time/cost distributions instead of Figure 4's temporal performance comparison. These changes modestly weaken reproducibility guidance and navigation; the metadata and layout updates provide no substantial offsetting quality gain.
